=={{header|Omegese}}==
{{works with|omc|sha256 2c824805, aien-dev/omega-mv e5b32567, Linux AArch64}}
Omega has no imports, so the small output helpers (<code>emit</code> and friends) are part of the program.
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
om2
text nl "\n"
text sp " "
text minus "-"
text tm "matrix:\n"
text tdet "determinant: "
text tper "permanent: "
text tdata "1 2 3 4 2 9 4 7 5 3 6 1 8 1 2 3 4 4 5 6 7 7 8 9 10 10 11 12 13"
global vals long 64
global mat long 25
global perm ulong 8
global res long 2
note emit writes every byte of a to stdout; a short write is retried, an error exits 1
fn emit a view uchar * to void
o = ulong 0
while lt o len a bound 4096
k = write 1 a o sub len a o
if le k 0
exit 1
end
o = add o ulong k
end
end
note emitu writes n in decimal; 20 digits hold every ulong
fn emitu n ulong to void
d = new uchar 20 0
i = ulong 20
v = n
while true bound 20
i = sub i 1
put d i uchar add rem v 10 48
v = div v 10
if eq v 0
break
end
end
emit part d i sub 20 i
end
note emiti writes a signed n; the magnitude is taken as a ulong so the minimum long cannot overflow
fn emiti n long to void
if lt n 0
emit minus
emitu add bitcast ulong not n 1
else
emitu ulong n
end
end
note emitwi writes a signed n right-aligned in w columns (w at most 20)
fn emitwi n long w ulong to void
d = new uchar 21 32
i = ulong 21
v = n
if lt n 0
v = neg n
end
while true bound 20
i = sub i 1
put d i uchar add long 48 rem v 10
v = div v 10
if eq v 0
break
end
end
if lt n 0
i = sub i 1
put d i 45
end
if gt w sub 21 i
i = sub 21 w
end
emit part d i sub 21 i
end
note parse reads the decimal numbers in s (separated by spaces, an optional - sign) into vals and
note returns how many; one pass over s, so the loop is bounded by len s
fn parse s view uchar * to ulong
n = ulong 0
v = long 0
sg = long 1
dig = false
for i ulong len s
c = get s i
if eq c 45
sg = long -1
else
if and ge c 48 le c 57
v = add mul v 10 long sub c 48
dig = true
else
if dig
put vals n mul sg v
n = add n 1
end
v = long 0
sg = long 1
dig = false
end
end
end
if dig
put vals n mul sg v
n = add n 1
end
ret n
end
note both are sums over all n! permutations p of the products m[0][p0] * .. * m[n-1][p(n-1)]; the
note determinant gives each the sign of p (its inversion count parity), the permanent adds them all
note nextp: the next permutation in lexicographic order, false after the last
fn nextp n ulong to bool
if lt n 2
ret false
end
i = sub n 1
while gt i 0 bound 8
if lt get perm sub i 1 get perm i
break
end
i = sub i 1
end
if eq i 0
ret false
end
j = sub n 1
while le get perm j get perm sub i 1 bound 8
j = sub j 1
end
t = get perm sub i 1
put perm sub i 1 get perm j
put perm j t
k = sub n 1
while lt i k bound 8
t2 = get perm i
put perm i get perm k
put perm k t2
i = add i 1
k = sub k 1
end
ret true
end
fn odd n ulong to bool
c = ulong 0
for i ulong n
for j ulong n
if and lt i j gt get perm i get perm j
c = add c 1
end
end
end
ret eq rem c 2 1
end
fn term n ulong to long
p = long 1
for i ulong n
p = mul p get mat add mul i n get perm i
end
ret p
end
note detper fills res[0] with the determinant and res[1] with the permanent; 5! = 120 bounds the loop
fn detper n ulong to void
for i ulong n
put perm i i
end
put res 0 0
put res 1 0
while true bound 120
t = term n
put res 1 add get res 1 t
if odd n
put res 0 sub get res 0 t
else
put res 0 add get res 0 t
end
if not nextp n
break
end
end
end
fn case o ulong n ulong to void
emit tm
for i ulong n
for j ulong n
put mat add mul i n j get vals add o add mul i n j
emitwi get mat add mul i n j 4
end
emit nl
end
detper n
emit tdet
emiti get res 0
emit nl
emit tper
emiti get res 1
emit nl
end
note the 5 x 5 case is 0 .. 24, filled in place rather than parsed
fn main to int
n = parse tdata
case 0 2
case 4 3
case 13 4
for i ulong 25
put vals add 29 i long i
end
case 29 5
ret 0
end
</syntaxhighlight>
